articles.title: Mining project near India's first marine sanctuary, national park gets nod
articles.description: A key clearance has been given to a bauxite and marl mining project in Gujarat's Devbhumi Dwarka district, nearly 1.6 and six kilometres from India's first marine wildlife sanctuary and first marine national park, respectively, on the Gulf of Kachchh's southern shore. While the marine wildlife sanctuary (spread over 458 square kilometre) was established in 1980, the marine national park (spanning 168 square kilometre) was created two years later to protect and conserve marine flora and fauna. According to Gujarat's forest and environment department, a complex coral reef ecosystem and extensive mangroves dominate the seascape of the marine park's shallow water, and the eco-system hosts diverse species. Mining has been proposed to take place at the Mevasa Block in an area spanning over five hectares (ha). articles.title: UPI To Remain Free For Users, But Some Merchants May Face Nominal Fees In Future: Govt
articles.description: The Government of India has clarified that users will not have to pay transaction charges for UPI payments, while a nominal Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) could be introduced for a limited set of merchant transactions in the future. The clarification came a day after the Lok Sabha passed a Bill amending the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, enabling charges on UPI and other notified electronic payments. The Finance Ministry said Person-to-Person transactions will remain free, while most merchant transactions will also continue without charges. Any future MDR would be threshold-based, nominal and lower than card transaction rates. The government said the amendment aims to support UPI’s long-term sustainability, cybersecurity, infrastructure and innovation. It also rejected claims of external influence, calling them unfounded, false and misleading.
